clue.text: End with drink for your health

parts.note: the bottom is the end of something
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone finishing the evening with one last drink, raised to good health.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTOM and SUP run together as BOTTOMS UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are toasts said on raising a glass, wishing the company well before drinking.

clue.text: Architectural feature however comes with lock

parts.note: but is a synonym of however
a lock of hair is a tress

explanation.surface: An awkward sentence about a building detail that somehow involves a lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door, but here it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A buttress is a projecting support built against a wall, a standard structural element in architecture.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rubbish dump, in British usage

explanation.surface: Advice to throw something away.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a tip is also the local rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a waste-disposal site in British English and a useful hint or suggestion.

clue.text: First of oranges, as it happens, green or black fruit

indicators.note: first of tells us to take only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: opening letter of oranges
a live broadcast is shown as it happens

explanation.surface: A fruit bowl note: oranges first, then a fruit that may be green or black.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are fruit picked either unripe and green or ripe and dark, hence both colours.

clue.text: Utter genius, an unusual melody on telly, say

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters before it are put in an unexpected new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Praise for a composer's strange but brilliant theme for a television show.
explanation.definitionFit: A signature tune is the theme that identifies a programme, such as one on television.

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the following word

parts.note: pluck is bravery

indicators.note: something turned round faces the other way, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who turned to bravery when taking a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned to' reads like a phrase meaning resorted to, but 'turned' acts on 'to' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking pot luck means taking whatever chance brings, without choice or planning.

clue.text: One carried by wings of that bird

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it
the wings of something are its two edges, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of that
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single creature borne aloft on a bird's wings.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside TT to give TIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tits are small songbirds, such as the blue tit common in British gardens.

clue.text: Pound to soften blow I resented

indicators.note: to blow something is to wreck it, so the following letters are scattered and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone resented a blow that was meant to make them softer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tenderise meat is to beat it with a mallet so it becomes less tough.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pastry case with sweet filling

explanation.surface: A pudding with a tangy flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a pastry pudding and an adjective for an acidic, sour flavour.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: excellent, in old-fashioned British slang
second meaning: something spread on top of food

explanation.surface: Delight at some splendid cake icing.
explanation.walkthrough: Spiffing and topping are both dated upper-class British words for excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: Icing is one example of a layer put on top of a cake, and the same word is old slang for first-rate.

clue.text: Singer right one time after reflecting

indicators.note: a reflection shows things the other way round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A vocalist who, on reflection, got it right for once.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, a part in choral music.

clue.text: Weapon discovered in car, I fled

indicators.note: something discovered in the words is sitting inside them

parts.note: found within the letters of car, I fled

explanation.surface: A getaway driver confessing that a gun was found in their car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, one kind of weapon.

parts.note: flash means showy
a back is a defensive player in football or rugby

explanation.surface: Recalling a showy footballer in defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashback is a vivid recollection of a past event that comes back abruptly.

clue.text: Shoe found in centre of path, charming object

indicators.note: found in places the preceding word inside the selected letters
the centre of a word is its middle letters, so only those are kept

parts.note: the two middle letters of path
a mule is a backless slipper or shoe

explanation.surface: A shoe lying on a path turns out to be a lucky charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' is a pun: an amulet is a charm. A mule is a backless shoe, not only an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off harm, so it is literally an object with a charm.

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing supporting another sits beneath it, fixing the order of the parts

parts.note: to egg on is to spur on, so eggs means spurs
a hellish experience is a nightmare

explanation.surface: A dreadful season for Tottenham Hotspur fans with a grim end to the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'supporting' puts HELL under EGGS. Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshell is a type of paint finish with a slight sheen, so it is one sort of finish.

clue.text: Bold son was foolish ultimately, breaking under pressure

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of foolish
something buckling is giving way under strain

explanation.surface: A daring son who, in the end, acted foolishly and cracked under stress.
explanation.definitionFit: Swashbuckling describes daring, adventurous behaviour like that of a film pirate.

clue.text: Thrones designed for some queens and workers?

indicators.note: something designed is made up to a new plan, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Seats of state made for royalty and their staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Queens and workers suggest monarchs and servants, but they are castes in an insect colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornet nest has queens and workers, like other social wasps, so these are examples.

clue.text: Price to pay for what bull might do?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to rush forward in attack

explanation.surface: Wondering what it costs to see a bull in action.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a fee demanded and a verb for rushing headlong at something, as a bull does.

indicators.note: part of tells us the letters are a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: found within the letters of compadre's split

explanation.surface: Splitting the work rota of a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shift' looks like a work period, but a shift is also a loose, simple dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a straight, loose-fitting dress, so the general garment defines it.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: went out with someone romantically

explanation.surface: Someone removed an old hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To have dated someone is to have taken them out, and something dated is no longer fashionable.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sport played on horseback
second meaning: Marco ..., the Venetian traveller

explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team sport played on horseback, and Marco Polo travelled from Venice to China.

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to rate is to class or grade

explanation.surface: Phoning a class to give them a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call, but it is the letter shaped like a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to deliver a formal address, which is making a speech.

indicators.note: twisting something bends it out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
wine is a drink

explanation.surface: Instructions for loosening a bolt, followed by a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The nut in the surface is a bolt fitting, but only its three letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: To untwine is to unwind or free something that was twisted together.

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: opening letters of in Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An ancient emperor's famous fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is a literary word for anger, the same as wrath.

parts.note: oi is a call to get attention
K is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone scolding a spoilt young monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: An oik is British slang for a crude or badly behaved person.
explanation.definitionFit: Oik is a British insult for an ill-mannered youth, close to a brat.

parts.note: to speed is to run fast
well means successfully

explanation.surface: Instructions to grow a plant or perhaps to operate one successfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' looks like a factory or a verb, but it is the definition: speedwell is a small blue wild flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedwell is a low-growing flowering plant of the genus Veronica, with small blue blooms.
